A 59-year-old male patient on the surgical floor develops new abdominal discomfort and bloating 48
hours after undergoing an uncomplicated right hemicolectomy. He has not passed flatus or stool since
the procedure. His vital signs include a heart rate of 110/min, blood pressure of 128/54 mmHg,
respiratory rate of 17/min, and temperature of 37.2 °C (99.0 °F). On examination, his abdomen is
distended, mildly tender, tympanic to percussion, and has diminished bowel sounds. A peripheral IV is
placed, and IV fluids are administered. What is the most appropriate next step in managing this
patient? Answer Choices: (A) Initiate total parenteral nutrition (B) Administer opioid analgesics for pain
relief (C) Examine the surgical wounds (D) Measure serum lactate levels (E) Obtain an abdominal
X-ray (F) Perform an exploratory laparotomy (G) Start broad-spectrum antibiotics (H) Administer
prokinetic agents (I) Insert a nasogastric tube (J) Perform a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis

A. Administer opioid analgesics for pain relief
B. Initiate total parenteral nutrition
C. Perform a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis
D. Insert a nasogastric tube
E. Start broad-spectrum antibiotics
F. Administer prokinetic agents
G. Perform an exploratory laparotomy
H. Obtain an abdominal X-ray
I. Examine the surgical wounds
J. Measure serum lactate levels
